questions.prompt: A C program calls printf(). What is the FIRST thing that runs after the call?
options: Code in the standard C library, in user mode

questions.prompt: The library is about to make the write() system call. What does it put where the kernel expects it?
options: write()'s system-call number and its parameters

questions.prompt: What switches the CPU from user mode to kernel mode for a system call?
In kernel mode, how does the system-call interface choose the code to run?
options: It searches by the function's name
It indexes the system-call table by the call's number
It runs every system call in turn

questions.prompt: When the kernel's write() finishes, control returns to the C library and then to the program, back in user mode.
A system call takes 8 parameters on a machine with 6 parameter registers. What will a Linux-style library most likely do?
options: Run the call in user mode
Put the parameters in a block in memory and pass its address in a register

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: printf() is a library call, and write() is a ______ call. (one word)
Which part of this path would change if you moved a POSIX program from Linux to macOS?
options: The program's calls to read() and write()
The system-call numbers and kernel implementations, which the API hides
